what: MeikiOCR (rtr46/meikiocr 0.3.5: local, CPU, offline) added to the CLANNAD comparison of eval/clannad_refs_protocol.json (owner request 2026-10-14): (a) its recognizer on the same stored GRAD line crops as every other arm, scored line by line against the frozen references, paired with VOCR3_W20 and Lens; (b) its own detection plus recognition on the full stored screens, scored per screen (whole dialogue) against the same references, kept apart from (a). Model size and host speed for context.
use: report only: CLANNAD is a protected test title. Nothing here chooses, tunes, calibrates, qualifies or drops a model, threshold, finder or recipe. MeikiOCR runs with its package defaults, fixed in this file before any MeikiOCR read of a CLANNAD crop or frame. The references are the frozen ones of eval/clannad_refs_protocol.json and are not changed. Nothing leaves this machine: no hosted API, no Codex, no third party.

references.freeze: WORK/refs.freeze.json, frozen 2026-10-14T03:04:39Z: refs_sha256 35411688749b2968b4b47306b65475503644c0bfa1ea8eba0b30885fe4a6212b, lines_sha256 a6be0300b651a2cdf3ae58f9705b6f100263b66b7030365b119e6a0a2323ffd1, protocol_sha256 3b86ca54b6cf88099950c89cbae1e9bd9eca8e5333316d6729fd62ca2be8d5a0 (eval/clannad_refs_protocol.json, unchanged)
references.entanglement: MeikiOCR's recognizer is one of the two labelling engines whose readings were R1's candidates (teacher/engines.Meiki: run_recognition with punct_conf_factor 0.2, owocr's setting; listed first on each R1 entry), and its reading was among R2's and R3's unattributed candidates. A reference can therefore lean towards MeikiOCR's reading where a read accepted a plausible but wrong candidate: arm (a)'s scores can be optimistic against every system that was not an R1 candidate, and arm (b) uses the same recognizer. Reported with the counts in whole_dialogue.entanglement_counts; never corrected.

engine.package: meikiocr 0.3.5 from PyPI: wheel meikiocr-0.3.5-py3-none-any.whl sha256 5d1ede4bcf46ecf17ef9a59db26edbc3e622aa3ed3c27bb64317077abbe2fccb. Its three modules equal https://github.com/rtr46/meikiocr commit 52aa607ecdc1038c7bf390f37cd9a8b306e8a08a (git blob sha1: meikiocr/__init__.py ad94604546562f32428428450fecc24b931bdd66, meikiocr/cli.py d8234e41628dd76785cc8771b207d1e3a31476b7, meikiocr/ocr.py 2fd63c6716fdc6b64b0c76a8ea3852abf9b49427) once the wheel's CRLF line endings are read as LF; `clannad_meiki.py verify` checks this and records it
engine.env: .venv-meiki: uv venv --python 3.11.15, then uv pip sync --require-hashes eval/clannad_meiki_requirements.lock (onnxruntime 1.30.0, numpy 2.4.6, opencv-python-headless 5.0.0.93, huggingface-hub 0.36.2, pillow 12.3.0: teacher/requirements.lock's versions; onnx 1.18.0 only counts parameters)
engine.models_source: the teacher's pinned copies in $HERD/shared/artifacts/teacher/models (teacher/engines.PINS; read only, reused, not copied). They are the files meikiocr 0.3.5 downloads by default (ocr.DET_MODEL_REPO / REC_MODEL_REPO at main, whose heads on 2026-10-14 are the pinned revisions; Hugging Face's LFS sha256 equals each pin). Every load checks the sha256.
engine.sessions: meikiocr's own MeikiOCR methods (run_recognition, run_detection, run_ocr) on an instance whose three sessions are made with meikiocr's own options (ORT_ENABLE_ALL, intra- and inter-op spinning off) on CPUExecutionProvider, plus intra_op_num_threads 1 and inter_op_num_threads 1 (meikiocr's __init__ would take every core; heavy.sh gives 5 threads per slot), and max_batch_size 8 (its default). Nothing else differs from MeikiOCR().
engine.offline: every MeikiOCR run inside `unshare -rn` (no network) with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, through heavy.sh; up to 5 single-thread worker processes in one slot

arm_a.name: MeikiOCR
arm_a.input: every line of WORK/lines.jsonl (4,271 on 2,177 pages): the stored processed line PNG (grey, the C GRAD finder's crop, dark text inverted once), file hash checked (clannad_refs.load_grey), as three identical channels; the same pixels as every protocol arm and Lens
arm_a.call: MeikiOCR.run_recognition([crop], conf_threshold=0.1, punct_conf_factor=1.0)[0]['text']: the package defaults; a crop taller than it is wide goes to the vertical recognizer, as meikiocr decides; no post-processing
arm_a.output: DIR/arms.meiki.jsonl and DIR/arms.meiki.meta.json in clannad_refs's extra-arm format (suffix meiki), written exclusively and only once WORK/refs.freeze.json exists; DIR = $HERD/shared/private/meiki-clannad (chmod 700)
arm_a.score: .venv-ci/bin/python eval/clannad_refs.py score --work WORK --suffix meiki --into DIR --pair MeikiOCR:VOCR3_W20 --pair MeikiOCR:Lens --out eval/clannad_meiki_lines_20261014.json, once (clannad_refs's one attempt for the suffix): CER, exact and hiragana for every system, the name / not-name / inverted subsets, the no-text crops, the Lens proxy, page bootstrap and the two pairs, exactly as the protocol arms are scored

arm_b.name: MeikiOCR_screen
arm_b.input: one stored native frame per page of WORK/lines.jsonl: the page's source PNG (clannad_longrun.verified_image: file and decoded-pixel hashes), the frame the long run's finder read; RGB to BGR (meikiocr reads images as OpenCV BGR), an alpha channel dropped
arm_b.call: MeikiOCR.run_ocr(frame, det_threshold=0.5, rec_threshold=0.1, punct_conf_factor=1.0): the package and CLI defaults. Each result's line box is the return value of the one run_detection call run_ocr itself makes (seen through a pass-through wrapper on the instance, removed afterwards; no second detection pass); results and boxes pair by index, and their counts must match, else the run fails
arm_b.region: a detection is kept when its box centre ((x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2) lies in the long run's ROI (WORK/lines.meta.json roi [x, y, w, h] = [32, 360, 896, 184]; left and top edges inclusive, right and bottom exclusive): the region the GRAD finder scanned and the only region the references cover. Detections outside it are counted, never scored.
arm_b.output: DIR/screens.meiki.jsonl (private: boxes, texts, times) and DIR/screens.meiki.meta.json, written exclusively and only once WORK/refs.freeze.json exists

whole_dialogue.screens: the pages of WORK/lines.jsonl whose every crop is either a reference line (refs.jsonl status ref) or a crop two reads found empty (refs.jsonl notext). A page with any other excluded crop (cut, multi, unsure, ui, bad, two of three non-text, no two reads agree) is left out whole for every system and counted by reason. A page whose crops are all empty has no reference text: counted, with what each system writes on it, never in CER.
whole_dialogue.order: reading order, the same rule for every system and the references: boxes (native-frame coordinates) sorted by centre y; a box joins the current row when its vertical overlap with the row's span is at least half the smaller of the two heights, else it starts a row; rows top to bottom, boxes left to right (x0, then y0) within a row
whole_dialogue.reference: the page's reference lines in reading order by their crop boxes; a name line keeps its name flag
whole_dialogue.systems: MeikiOCR_screen: its kept detections' texts in reading order. On the GRAD crops: each system's readings of every crop of the page (reference lines and empty crops alike, what a whole-dialogue pipeline would output), in reading order by the crop boxes: MeikiOCR (arm a), every arm of eval/clannad_refs_protocol.json, and Lens
whole_dialogue.metric: train/general_vn_textbox_guard.transcript_score on the page's reference lines and the system's texts (one alignment of the joined normalised strings, eval/metrics.norm): all/full errors over all/full reference characters is the screen CER (primary); body/full (the names' characters left out of the denominator, every unmatched insertion charged to the body) is the dialogue-only CER; all/hira the hiragana; an exact screen is one whose joined normalised output equals its joined normalised reference
whole_dialogue.intervals: 95% percentile intervals from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of whole screens (sorted page ids, numpy default_rng(0)), as the line score
whole_dialogue.pairs_method: CAND - BASE in points: eval/vocr3_report.paired_bootstrap over screens for the screen CER (all/full) and the dialogue-only CER (body/full); the same resamples for exact screens
whole_dialogue.secondary: MeikiOCR_screen: detections in total, kept, outside the ROI, vertical; screens with no kept detection; characters it writes from kept detections that overlap no crop box of the page (an insertion against references that cover only the GRAD crops; some may be dialogue the finder missed)
whole_dialogue.entanglement_counts: lines where arm (a)'s text equals R1's MeikiOCR candidate (WORK/engines.jsonl meiki), over all lines and over the scored lines; scored lines whose reference key (teacher/vote.key) equals R1's MeikiOCR candidate key, and the same for PP-OCRv6 small; the same two counts on the lens-disagree lines
whole_dialogue.bias: the references cover only the text inside the GRAD finder's crops. Dialogue the finder missed or cut short counts against MeikiOCR_screen as insertions and against no GRAD-crop system, and pages with a cut or multi-line crop are left out whole. Both favour the GRAD-crop systems in (b).
whole_dialogue.command: .venv-ci/bin/python eval/clannad_meiki.py score-screens --work WORK --into DIR --out eval/clannad_meiki_screens_20261014.json, once (DIR/screens.score.attempt.json is created exclusively before any number is computed)

size: per model file: bytes, sha256, parameters (onnx initializers plus Constant node tensors) by dtype, input shape (`clannad_meiki.py resources`). The int8 MNN conversion's size (ports/meiki/dependencies.json) and the console times (notes/27-Meiki-hardware-and-project-lessons.md) are cited, not measured again.
speed: host only, never a console number (`clannad_meiki.py speed`): 200 line ids and 50 page ids drawn by random.Random(0).sample from the sorted ids (not by content); one thread; 5 warm-up calls; 3 repeats. MeikiOCR: run_recognition ms per line, run_detection and run_ocr ms per screen, model load. VOCR3_W20 and VOCR_H15: the same scalar C W8I library build as the arms (eval/vocr3_report.build_native, CReader.text), ms per line on the same crops, model load. CPU model and versions recorded. Report the median per call and each repeat's median.
public: counts, rates, intervals, hashes, sizes and times only (clannad_refs.assert_public on every public JSON); readings, references, boxes and frames stay under shared/private/
one_attempt: each score runs once; a failure is reported, not retried with changes
